fixes.rationale_full: Root fix per the hint, without a third per-spelling normalisation. Added AtomicFiles.directoryLockFor(File): a process-wide monitor keyed on the canonical path of the file's parent directory (own map DIRECTORY_LOCKS; IOException falls back to the absolute spelling). The file name is not part of the key, so no spelling the file system treats as one name (case, NFC/NFD, Windows short names, ./, .., symlinks) can split the monitor, and the key does not change across the first create (verified on this JDK/APFS: getCanonicalPath of an existing directory resolves NFD and case to the on-disk name). AtomicFiles.write and FileUserStore.commit (the only check-and-write holder) now synchronize on directoryLockFor instead of lockFor, so all writes into one directory are serialized; auth writes a few small files per directory so contention is negligible. Additive alternative to the hint where it conflicted with hard rule 2: making lockFor itself return the directory monitor would break the existing assertions assertNotSame(lockFor(users.json), lockFor(groups.txt)) in lockForKeysOnTheCanonicalPath and assertNotSame(before, lockFor(users.json.bak)) in lockForFoldsTheCaseOfAFileThatDoesNotExistYet, so lockFor is kept unchanged (per-path key, case-folded) and its Javadoc now says writes hold directoryLockFor instead; it is not nested inside write because holding lockFor then taking the directory monitor would invert the lock order and could deadlock. Temp/staging naming: the staging directory .<name>.tmp.new-<hex> was already unique per write; the <name>.tmp name is kept because it is asserted by AC1/tempFileIsOwnerOnlyBeforeItIsOpenedForWriting, FileUserStoreTest and Wave11DoctorTest and is what the doctor's file-state check looks for; two spellings can no longer share it concurrently because every write into the directory holds one monitor. Tests: the existing case race body moved unchanged (same assertions, 60 rounds) into a helper assertRacingFirstCreatesLoseNothing(nameA, nameB, rounds); new racingFirstCreatesThroughUnicodeNormalizationSpellingsLoseNothing (red test, assumes a normalization-insensitive FS by probe) and directoryLockForIsIndependentOfTheNameSpelling (NFC, NFD, case, ./, .., symlink, same before and after the first create, a subdirectory differs). The earlier case race and the ./ / symlink lockFor tests stay green. Docs ko+en line 747 now describe per-directory serialization including NFC/NFD.

public_api_changes: Added public static Object AtomicFiles.directoryLockFor(File) in internal package com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth.internal (additive; not a documented user API). AtomicFiles.lockFor(File) unchanged in signature and key semantics; it is no longer held by write or FileUserStore.
